title: DPA: Inference Query Sampling & Redaction Procedure - Annex
body:
Purpose:
This Annex is intended to sit alongside a standard Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and to specify operational procedures and contractual commitments for sampling, retaining, redacting, and making available inference queries ("queries") and their transient artifacts produced by Redwood Inference when providing inference services to Customers. It defines minimum controls, evidence, and escalation steps that the vendor will adhere to for regulated or high-sensitivity workloads.

Scope:
Applies to all inference requests routed to Redwood-hosted or Redwood-managed Dedicated/Private inference endpoints where Customer elects to enable sampling, debugging, or quality monitoring features that capture textual query content, tokens, or model outputs. Does not change core data residency or purpose limitations in the primary DPA; it supplements them with operational mechanics for sampling and redaction.

Definitions (selected):
- "Query": any request payload or associated metadata sent to an inference endpoint (text, structured prompt, attachments).
- "Sampled Artifact": a stored copy of a Query and/or generated output captured for debugging, quality monitoring, or compliance review per this Annex.
- "Redaction": deterministic removal or masking of sensitive elements from a Sampled Artifact according to agreed rules.
- "Ephemeral Buffer": in-memory or short-lived storage used for streaming inference; not considered persistent unless expressly captured as a Sampled Artifact.

Principles:
1) Minimize: Only sample the minimal subset of fields required for the stated monitoring purpose.
2) Protect: All Sampled Artifacts must be encrypted at rest and in transit and tagged with retention and access metadata.
3) Traceable deletion: Deletions of Sampled Artifacts must generate an auditable evidence record.
4) Least privilege: Access for review or reconstitution of sampled content is role-bound and logged.

Sampling Controls (operational commitments):
- Sampling Rates: Default sampling is off. If enabled, Customer and Redwood will agree on a sampling rate (e.g., 0.1% of total requests or 1 in 1,000) and sample selection method (randomized versus triggered by error patterns).
- Triggered Sampling: Redwood may enable triggered sampling for requests matching error classes (timeouts, model failures) or where Customer provides a trigger rule. Triggered samples must be scoped to the minimum data required for root cause analysis.
- Field-level Selection: Sampling must support selecting specific fields (e.g., "prompt_text", "metadata.job_id") to avoid capturing unnecessary PII.

Redaction and Transformation Requirements:
- Automated Redaction: Before persisting any Sampled Artifact containing user-provided text, Redwood will apply an automated redaction pipeline that: 1) runs configured pattern detectors for phone numbers, email addresses, SSNs, credit card numbers, and common PII; 2) normalizes and replaces detected tokens with deterministic placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_1>, <PHONE_1>); 3) records redaction transforms in metadata for auditability.
- Customer Allowlist/Blocklist: Customer can supply a list of tokens or regex patterns to always redact or to explicitly allow (allowlist) if they accept responsibility. Redwood will not enable an allowlist that weakens explicit regulatory obligations.
- Manual Escalation Redaction: If a Sampled Artifact is escalated for human review, reviewers will only receive the redacted view unless Customer grants narrow, time-bound exceptions and those exceptions are logged and approved by Customer security contact.

Retention, Deletion, and Evidence:
- Retention Windows: Default retention for redacted Sampled Artifacts is 30 days. For compliance or debugging engagements, retention may be extended by written agreement (maximum 180 days unless mutually agreed and documented).
- Proof of Deletion: Upon deletion request (by Customer or per retention expiry), Redwood will emit a deletion certificate containing: artifact id(s), timestamps for deletion request and completion, storage location identifiers, and the secure wipe method used. Certificates will be retained for 24 months for audit purposes.
- Immediate Deprovisioning: For emergency takedowns (e.g., legal hold conflicts, PII leakage), Redwood will isolate relevant artifacts and present an evidence ledger to Customer within 48 hours; remediation steps and final disposition will be documented within 10 business days.

Access Controls and Logging:
- Roles and Approval: Access for sampled artifact review requires a documented justification and approval flow. Approved roles include: Security Engineer, Privacy SME, and Support Engineer (narrowed). All approvals are recorded in the access log.
- Session Recording: All human sessions that view sampled artifacts must be logged, including viewer identity, reason, and a snapshot hash of the redacted artifact viewed.
- Break-glass: Emergency "break-glass" access is permitted only with two-factor approval (on-call manager + Customer emergency contact) and is automatically revoked after the stated emergency window.

Audit and Evidence Production:
- Quarterly Evidence Pack: Redwood will provide Customers with a quarterly evidence pack showing sampling rates, sample identifiers, retention state, deletion certificates, and anonymized access logs covering the quarter.
- On-demand Audit: Customer audit requests (reasonable scope) will be responded to within 15 business days. If forensic inspection requires full (non-redacted) artifacts, Redwood will require a narrow, signed request and may require lawful process where appropriate.

Security, Encryption, and Key Management:
- Encryption: All stored Sampled Artifacts are encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent. Keys are managed in a vendor KMS unless Customer elects a BYOK configuration for Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Key Rotation and Records: Redwood will rotate keys per internal policy (90–180 day windows) and record key version metadata linked to artifact ids to preserve the ability to verify deletion or produce required artifacts if authorized.

Third-party Processors and Subprocessors:
- Subprocessor Notification: Redwood will list subprocessors involved in storage or access of sampled artifacts. For any new subprocessor materially affecting sampled artifacts, Redwood will notify Customer 30 days in advance and provide an opportunity to object.

Breach and Incident Handling:
- Notification: If sampled artifacts are subject to unauthorized access or exfiltration, Redwood will notify Customer within 48 hours of detection with an initial triage report and a remediation timeline.
- Forensics: Redwood will preserve relevant evidence and provide a forensic summary and deletion/mitigation plan.

Contractual Clauses (template language excerpt to include in DPA Annex):
"Vendor agrees to only capture and retain Sampled Artifacts as expressly authorized by Customer and in accordance with the sampling, redaction, retention, deletion, and access rules set forth in this Annex. Vendor shall implement and maintain reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for Sampled Artifacts, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and audit logging. Upon Customer request or at the end of the retention period, Vendor shall promptly delete Sampled Artifacts and provide a deletion certificate. Exceptions to redaction or retention limits must be agreed in writing and documented in the quarterly evidence pack."

Operational Implementation Notes (for internal ops teams):
- Toggleability: Sampling must be feature-flag controlled per-customer and per-route.
- Metadata Schema: Each Sampled Artifact must include: artifact_id, route, tenant_id, sampling_reason, redaction_level, retention_expiry, storage_bucket_tag, encryption_key_id, created_by_proc.
- Indexing: Index only metadata to support search and deletion by artifact_id; the redacted payload should not be indexed with free-text search unless explicitly enabled and approved.

Appendix A — Example Redaction Workflow:
1) Request arrives -> route-level sampling rule evaluates -> sample selected.
2) Redaction pipeline runs in transient worker: PII detectors -> token replacement -> generate transform map.
3) Persist redacted artifact to encrypted store; write artifact metadata to index.
4) If escalated, route request through approval UI which records reviewer id and view snapshot.
5) On retention expiry, run deletion job, then emit deletion certificate.

Appendix B — Customer Checklist to Enable Sampling:
- Confirm sampling rate and justification.
- Provide allowlist/blocklist patterns if needed.
- Designate Customer security contact and emergency contact.
- Agree retention extension if required for debugging.

Exceptions and Negotiability:
- Customers in regulated jurisdictions may require modifications to retention caps or manual review thresholds; such deviations must be captured in a signed addendum.
- BYOK for artifact encryption is available for Dedicated/Private but requires additional operational onboarding and audit evidence.
